policy: Comparison traditions attach to existing writing identities. These records identify candidate witness collections and limits; they do not assert that every passage survives or authorize reconstruction without exact passage and source-coordinate verification.

records.date_of_witness_or_tradition: Physical manuscript generally dated 2nd–1st century BCE; exact passage-level use requires catalogue verification.
records.evidence_status: Known ancient Greek witness; exact coverage must be checked against edition and images.
records.coverage_limitations: Do not assume all of Deuteronomy survives. No passage may be supplied until exact extant fragments and source coordinates are mapped.
records.editorial_rule: Treat as a Greek manuscript witness, not as the entire Septuagint or as a Hebrew DSS reading.

records.date_of_witness_or_tradition: Physical codex commonly dated 4th century CE.
records.evidence_status: Major surviving Greek codex; exact book and folio coverage must be checked.
records.coverage_limitations: Confirm each passage is present in the codex and distinguish lacunae, corrections, and textual variants.
records.editorial_rule: Use only for the exact passage represented; retain Greek wording and identify translation-mediated readings.

records.date_of_witness_or_tradition: The textual tradition is ancient; surviving complete codices are medieval. Date each physical manuscript independently.
records.evidence_status: Independent Pentateuch textual tradition; not a single dated manuscript.
records.coverage_limitations: Applies only to the Five Books of Moses. Do not extend it to Joshua or Samuel. Qumran pre-Samaritan witnesses are separate DSS records.
records.editorial_rule: Keep Samaritan readings distinct from DSS pre-Samaritan texts and Masoretic readings.

records.evidence_status: Complete surviving Masoretic codex witness for the collection it transmits.
records.coverage_limitations: One medieval Masoretic witness. Its book division does not define archive scope. Map each passage and retain vocalization, marginal notes, and corrections.
records.editorial_rule: Do not project its wording backward as the exact reading of a DSS manuscript.

records.date_of_witness_or_tradition: Physical codex commonly dated circa 930 CE.
records.evidence_status: Important Masoretic codex; surviving portions include Prophets.
records.coverage_limitations: The codex is incomplete; the Pentateuch is not extant in the surviving codex. Verify relevant surviving folios before passage use.
records.editorial_rule: Do not claim it supplies a passage unless the relevant surviving folio is verified.

records.witness_or_collection: Ethiopic / Ge'ez scriptural translation tradition; individual codices not yet registered
records.date_of_witness_or_tradition: Translation tradition is ancient; surviving manuscript dates vary and must be recorded per codex.
records.evidence_status: Tradition-level candidate only; no individual manuscript verified in this record.
records.coverage_limitations: This is not a physical manuscript citation and cannot supply text. Identify a specific Ge'ez codex, edition, source language, and passage before use.
records.editorial_rule: Never label a Ge'ez translation as an original Hebrew or Greek manuscript reading.
